Metadata.title: Hissiyat | Research workspace
Metadata.description: Investigate online human experiences using transparent, source-specific research.

ai.title: AI Research Interpretation
ai.intro: Generate a local interpretation from the verified aggregate evidence for this research.
ai.fictional: Fictional research example · No real participant text
ai.sourceGrounded: Interpretation uses the completed research package.
ai.waiting: The CPU model may take a little time. You can continue reading the verified evidence below.
ai.needsEvidence: Complete a topic or event research run with the local AI feature enabled. Browser-only CSV imports currently retain their own analysis view.
ai.generatedBy: Generated by a local language model
ai.insufficient: Evidence is insufficient for a thematic interpretation.
ai.observations: These observations come from application computations. The model explains selected evidence; the application binds its references.
ai.verification: Automatic checks verify scope, references and numerical consistency and reject known unsupported claims. Semantic errors and missed implications remain possible.

facts.sample: Upstream matches or returned records {retrieved}. Selected documents {selected}. Analyzed documents {analyzed}.
facts.source_scope: Selection cap {limit}. Examined source rows {examined}. Eligible before sampling {eligible}.
facts.coverage: Observed publication coverage {first}–{last}, across {days} active UTC dates.
facts.temporal_comparison: Comparable sampling across time has not been established. Observed date coverage alone supports no trend comparison.
facts.no_expression_matches: No supported expression rule matched in {count} documents. Expressions may still be present.
facts.topic_partition: {method} analyzed {count} documents. Group sizes {sizes}. Unassigned {unassigned}. Cosine silhouette {silhouette} over {assigned} assigned documents.
facts.topic_validity: Thematic validity has no independent assessment. Group numbers and recurring terms are exploratory.
facts.topics_unavailable: There are too few eligible or distinct documents to establish the requested grouping.
facts.expression_validity: Rule precision and recall have no independent accuracy estimate.
facts.analysis_unavailable: Text analysis was not requested for this result.
facts.search_summary: Verified period coverage {first}–{last}. Nonzero observations {nonzero}, ambiguous zeros {zero}, missing {missing}, suppressed {suppressed}. Endpoint direction {direction}.
facts.search_unverified: The API response has unverified measurement or display semantics. Its structure supports no search-interest interpretation.
facts.search_limits: Search interest provides no absolute counts or measurement of emotions, opinions or causation. Zeros may reflect low volume or privacy suppression.
facts.context: Demographics and article context are unavailable.
facts.generalization: This selected sample supports no population or causal inference.

errors.model_unavailable: The local model is unavailable. Check its local runtime and backend configuration.
errors.model_timeout: Local generation exceeded its time limit. The verified evidence remains available.
errors.unsupported_claim: The model produced an unsupported claim. Its interpretation was withheld.

errors.evidence_expired: This evidence package is no longer available in the current backend session.
errors.busy: Another local analysis is running. Wait for it to finish.

policyComparison.title: Historical text comparison
policyComparison.scope: One verified Civil Comments/Jigsaw split with 97,320 rows, English wording filters and the fixed 2015–2017 UTC window. The two prespecified questions describe separate samples.
policyComparison.policies: Legacy uses the 500-character limit and explicit_english_rules_v1. Updated uses the 8,000-character limit and explicit_english_spans_v2. Both keep the same safety filters, deterministic sampling, 100-document cap and four-comment article cap.
policyComparison.selection: The samples share {shared, number} selected documents. {legacy_only, number} appear only in legacy and {updated_only, number} only in updated.
policyComparison.paired: On the same {documents, number} analyzed documents, legacy matched {legacy_detected_documents, number} and updated matched {updated_detected_documents, number}.
policyComparison.pairedCaution: This shared-document comparison measures rule changes. Full-sample counts also reflect the changed document selection. Additional matches require thematic validation.
policyComparison.evidence: Updated matched {documents, number} of {denominator, number} documents with {spans, number} evidence spans. {late, number} documents have evidence starting at or beyond character 500.
policyComparison.abstentions: Sentence abstentions include {quoted, number} quoted and {ambiguous, number} ambiguous or overly long contexts, plus {limited, number} evidence-limit stops.
policyComparison.categories: Inspect expression categories and rule evidence
policyComparison.categoryDenominators: Document denominators are {legacy, number} for legacy and {updated, number} for updated.
policyComparison.unsupported: A dash marks a category or measure unsupported by the legacy method. Categories overlap and each counts a document once.
policyComparison.pairedCategories: Changes per category within the {count, number} shared documents
policyComparison.changes: {gained, number} newly matched, {lost, number} no longer matched, {retained, number} matched by both
policyComparison.qualityCaution: Silhouette describes separation in each method’s representation. Low separation, a group under 10% and weak between-method ARI can leave common topic structure unverified. The k=3 rows are the prespecified sensitivity check.
policyComparison.availability: Primary model availability is {legacy} for legacy and {updated} for updated.
policyComparison.limitations: These are exploratory wording matches in selected historical comments. Article context and author geography are unknown. False positives and missed expressions remain possible. No additional human validation was performed. Zero matches leave the underlying experience unknown.
policyComparison.normalization: Legacy collapses whitespace. Updated retains paragraph breaks. Both topic comparisons use the current complete-document and segment-aggregation implementation. Earlier pilot model outputs retain their own historical protocol.

documentEvidence.heading: Documents and expression evidence
documentEvidence.processing: {documents, number} documents, {segments, number} processing segments and {characters, number} characters entered the analysis. {skipped, number} input records were excluded.
documentEvidence.method: Method explicit_english_spans_v2. Every category counts each document at most once. Matching sentences have named rules and original character spans.
documentEvidence.limits: Limits are 8,000 characters per document, 100,000 per collection, 100 documents and 1,200 processing segments. Segments are at most 400 characters. A document that exceeds a limit is excluded in full. Topic groups count documents.
documentEvidence.sourceWithheld: Source text is withheld. The document reference and span identify the evidence within the analyzed input.
documentEvidence.abstentions: {count, number} sentence or evidence-limit abstentions were recorded. Quotes, ambiguous context and overly long sentences can prevent a match.
documentEvidence.separation: {method} cosine silhouette {score} over {count, number} documents. This describes separation in that method’s representation.
documentEvidence.weakSeparation: The silhouette was at most 0.10 for {methods}. Groups overlap in that representation. A common interpretable topic structure remains unverified.

rules.direct_request_v2: Direct request addressed to another person
rules.explicit_reason_v1: First-person action with an explicit because clause

TopicResearch.title: Create Research
TopicResearch.intro: Investigate a topic or event through public discussions, with the search scope and limits visible at each step.
TopicResearch.topicHelp: Enter the words you want the source to search. Use 2–120 characters.
TopicResearch.eventHelp: Enter distinctive words from the event. Matches depend on the source search index.
TopicResearch.dateHelp: UTC dates, both inclusive. Select up to 31 days.
TopicResearch.civilHelp: English-language comments from news sites, 2015–2017. Source, sampling, safety limits and aggregate evidence are shown.
TopicResearch.civilScopeHelp: Enter an English word or exact phrase. Separate two to eight alternatives with |. Each alternative uses two to six words. A match only establishes that the wording appears in the comment.
TopicResearch.civilLiteral: Match type: literal word or phrase ({phrases}). The search ignores letter case and repeated whitespace.
TopicResearch.civilAnyPhrase: Match type: any of these exact phrases ({phrases}). Each comment counts once, even if several phrases match.
TopicResearch.civilDistinct: In the sample of {count, number}, {articles, number} distinct known article IDs and {publications, number} distinct known publication IDs were observed.
TopicResearch.civilScreening: First screening reason per excluded match — length {length}, contact or markup patterns {privacy_or_markup}, English wording check {language}, moderation state {moderation}, safety labels {safety_labels}.
TopicResearch.fixedTopics: The comparison uses two groups per method. This setting does not establish how many themes the comments contain.
TopicResearch.unevenTopics: A group contains under 10% of assigned comments in {methods}. A small group can reflect unusual wording or a few records. Group sizes alone cannot establish a distinct theme.
TopicResearch.agreementEvidence: The Adjusted Rand Index is {score} across {count, number} common assignments. It compares grouping overlap and accounts for chance.
TopicResearch.weakAgreementEvidence: The methods agree little on which records belong together. A shared theme structure is unverified.
TopicResearch.noAgreementEvidence: There is no usable agreement score for this result.
TopicResearch.limitedTopicTerms: At least one occupied group had no recurring terms safe to show. The evidence is insufficient to describe that group’s theme.
TopicResearch.expressionBoundary: A wording match cannot establish a speaker’s emotion, experience or stance. Low counts can reflect the rule coverage.
TopicResearch.civilContextLimit: Article IDs link comments within the archive. Headlines and original discussion context are unavailable here, so phrase matches alone cannot establish relevance to a specific news event.
TopicResearch.civilDates: UTC publication dates, both inclusive. The historical scope is 2015–2017.
TopicResearch.civilCoverage: One pinned Jigsaw expanded test split. After filtering and deduplication, stable ordering by hashed comment ID selects up to 100 comments and up to four per article. Comments without an article ID share one four-comment limit.
TopicResearch.civilSafety: Approved comments with annotated low toxicity and zero explicit-content, obscenity, threat and severe-toxicity scores pass this screen. The English wording and contact-information checks are limited. Unsuitable or identifying text can evade screening.
TopicResearch.civilExcluded: Among literal matches, exclusions were outside the date window ({dates}), invalid ({invalid}), duplicate ({duplicates}), or screened out by content and metadata rules ({restricted}).
TopicResearch.civilEmpty: No comments in this archive split met the search and screening criteria.
TopicResearch.civilLimitations: These counts describe selected historical comments. The data cannot establish audience opinion, a current trend, event participation or country differences.
TopicResearch.civilTimeline: Selected archive comments per observed publication month (UTC). Months without sample records are omitted.
TopicResearch.civilContext: The dataset provides identifiers and publication times. Article titles and individual source links are unavailable in this split.
TopicResearch.civilMethodology: Local text grouping uses distinct, bounded English comments. Wording rules count explicit expressions per comment. Identifiers only describe the archive metadata. No comment text or individual cluster assignments are displayed.
TopicResearch.civilClaim: The pinned Civil Comments split yielded {matched, number} literal matches from {examined, number} rows. Of those matches, {eligible, number} met the criteria and {selected, number} were selected for the sample.
TopicResearch.wikiHelp: A single English Wikipedia talk page for studying technology-related discussion. Only evidence links and aggregates appear here.
TopicResearch.wikiScopeHelp: This pilot uses one fixed technology talk page and its identifiable comments.
TopicResearch.wikiDates: UTC dates filter one page snapshot. At most 25 detected comments enter the screening sample.
TopicResearch.wikiCoverage: One snapshot of the current talk page. Up to 25 DiscussionTools comment candidates are screened, prioritizing the newest dated comments within the chosen window. Archives and unsigned discussion are outside this sample.
TopicResearch.wikiSafety: Only plainly formatted comments of verified local origin pass screening. The English wording and personal-information checks are limited heuristics.
TopicResearch.wikiMethodology: Local models group the screened English texts. Wording rules count expressions per text. The latest page snapshot has no pinned revision. No source text, usernames, or individual assignments are displayed.
TopicResearch.interpretationType: Computed observations and linked evidence. Generative summaries are disabled.
TopicResearch.claimScope: {source} · {first} to {last} UTC. {eligible} of {checked} screened records met the evidence criteria.
TopicResearch.claimDenominator: Text measures use {count} distinct eligible English records. Topic sizes count group assignments. Expression counts measure explicit wording per record.
TopicResearch.claimTopics: {method} grouped the sample of {count} records into groups of {sizes}. Unassigned records {unassigned}.
TopicResearch.claimSignals: In {count} texts, wording rules matched {summary}. Categories can overlap.
TopicResearch.claimNoSignals: No supported wording rule matched in the {count} analyzed texts.
TopicResearch.claimTime: The timeline counts eligible records by publication day. A single bounded sample cannot establish a trend.
TopicResearch.blueskyHelp: Public search can be refused by the source. The provider may determine language using its own signals.
TopicResearch.lemmyHelp: Search one page of up to 25 recent posts or comments from public Lemmy.World communities. Dates are applied to the returned page. Language filtering is unavailable.
TopicResearch.lemmyQueryHelp: Use words or a phrase. Lemmy.World searches its own public communities using the words entered.
TopicResearch.trendsHelp: Run one owner-approved official API search for the selected term, country and months. The Explore CSV is available as a fallback.

officialTrends.termHelp: Use one plain search term. A live request requires the operator’s approval for the exact scope.
officialTrends.dateHelp: The API accepts month restrictions. Choose up to 12 completed months. The returned frequency may differ from the request’s month precision.
officialTrends.measurement: Measurement: consistently scaled search interest, verified for this response.
officialTrends.pointStates: Nonzero observations {nonzero, number}. Ambiguous zeros {zero, number}. Missing {missing, number}. Explicitly suppressed {suppressed, number}.
officialTrends.peak: Highest verified nonzero interest first occurs on {day}. This peak occurs in {count, number} periods.
officialTrends.noPeak: There is no verified nonzero observation from which to identify a peak.
officialTrends.increased: Interest rose from the first to the last verified nonzero observation.
officialTrends.decreased: Interest fell from the first to the last verified nonzero observation.
officialTrends.unchanged: The first and last verified nonzero observations show the same interest.
officialTrends.insufficient: At least two verified nonzero observations are needed to compare the endpoints.
officialTrends.withheld: Only the response structure is available. Observed geography, periods and scale require verified response documentation before analysis.
officialTrends.shape: First point field types · date {date} · value {value}
officialTrends.detectedFields: Recognized metadata field names {fields}. Their presence alone does not establish their meanings.
officialTrends.limits: Zeros may reflect insufficient search volume or privacy suppression. Search interest cannot establish reasons for searching, emotions or population opinion. Discussion counts are a separate measure.

importedTrends.linkScopeHelp: The Explore link fills the research term and dates. Set geography in Google Trends before downloading the CSV.
importedTrends.dateHelp: Use a custom range of at least 30 days ending before today. Dates are interpreted in UTC.
importedTrends.help: Use the original Turkish or English Interest over time CSV and its Explore link. The importer supports Web Search and All categories. A two-country file must come from one chart with the same term and dates.
importedTrends.sameChart: This is the unmodified CSV from the linked chart. Its data is allowed for my local research use.
importedTrends.source: Data source: Google Trends Explore · user-provided CSV
importedTrends.measurement: Search interest index (0–100 within this export)
importedTrends.actualRange: File contains {count, number} period starts from {start} to {end} UTC. Boundary periods may cover only part of the requested range.
importedTrends.sharedScale: The two country columns occupy the same Explore export and use its common scale. The chart uses matched dates and a shared axis.
importedTrends.singleScale: This scale belongs to this Explore export. Compare periods within it.
importedTrends.chartLabel: Relative Google search interest over time for {regions}
importedTrends.coverage: Numeric values {observed, number} of {total, number} periods. Blank {missing, number}. Below 1 {suppressed, number}.
importedTrends.extremes: Highest observed index {peak}, first on {peakDate} ({peaks, number} periods at this value). Lowest observed index {trough}, first on {troughDate} ({troughs, number} periods at this value).
importedTrends.increase: From the first numeric observation ({from}, {fromDate}) to the last ({to}, {toDate}), the index rose by {delta} points.
importedTrends.decrease: From the first numeric observation ({from}, {fromDate}) to the last ({to}, {toDate}), the index fell by {delta} points.
importedTrends.unchanged: The first numeric observation ({from}, {fromDate}) equals the last ({to}, {toDate}).
importedTrends.noObserved: There are no numeric observations in this series. Peaks, troughs and endpoint changes are unavailable.
importedTrends.compare: Across {aligned, number} of {total, number} periods with numeric values on both sides, {first} had the higher index in {leftHigher, number}, {second} in {rightHigher, number}, and the values were equal in {equal, number}.
importedTrends.noComparison: There are no periods with numeric observations for both countries.
importedTrends.limits: A numeric 0 is a reported value and may reflect low volume. Blanks and below-1 values are excluded from numeric summaries. Changes describe reported relative search activity. Reasons for searching and population sentiment remain unknown.
importedTrends.separate: Discussion activity counts records from its own source. Search interest is measured separately.
importedTrends.provenanceNote: CSV read in this tab. The link and headers describe the user-supplied export. The file hash identifies the exact bytes. Credit Google Trends when reusing the observations and follow Google’s terms.

errors.link: Enter a direct Google Trends Explore link. Import is available in the local preview at 127.0.0.1.
errors.scope: Use the same term and custom dates as the Explore link. This import supports Web Search, All categories and one geography or two countries in a single chart.
errors.file: The CSV file could not be read. Check the selected file and try again.
errors.encoding: This file contains invalid UTF-8. Check that you selected the original export.
errors.format: The CSV contains broken quotation marks, a row with the wrong number of cells, or invalid characters.
errors.structure: This chart format is unsupported. Select the original Turkish or English Interest over time export with All categories.
errors.metadata: The file’s term, geography, number of series or dates differ from the Explore link. Use the link from the same chart.
errors.parser: An unexpected error interrupted the import. If it recurs with the same file, report it as an application issue.
errors.periods: The file’s dates must form a continuous daily, weekly, monthly or yearly sequence.
errors.values: Allowed values are numeric indices from 0 to 100, a blank cell, or <1.
errors.size: Import a CSV with 1–2,000 periods and a file size of at most 256 KiB.

TopicResearch.fictionalHelp: Try the workflow with invented records in English or Turkish.
TopicResearch.unsupportedGeography: Discussion searches cannot filter by geography. The Trends export supplies its own geography.
TopicResearch.localOnly: Research searches are available in the opted-in local development preview.
TopicResearch.resultAnnouncement: {count} eligible records in the research results.
TopicResearch.fictionalCoverage: The fictional source matches the entered phrase in the selected window.
TopicResearch.blueskyCoverage: One page, ordered by latest in the Bluesky search index. Eligible posts are checked against their own UTC publication dates.
TopicResearch.lemmyCoverage: One page of the newest matching posts in Lemmy.World’s own communities. The date range is applied after retrieval. Replies and other instances are outside this sample.
TopicResearch.lemmyCommentsCoverage: One page of matching comments from Lemmy.World’s own public threads. Dates refer to the comments. The result does not cover complete threads or other instances.
TopicResearch.lemmySafety: Posts and communities flagged as adult or restricted, or missing the required safety flags, are excluded. Unflagged material can still be unsuitable.
TopicResearch.blueskySafety: Recognized adult and restriction labels are excluded when supplied. Unlabelled material can still be unsuitable.
TopicResearch.excluded: Excluded records by reason — outside dates {dates}, invalid {invalid}, duplicates {duplicates}, safety or visibility {restricted}.
TopicResearch.empty: No eligible records in this response. The source may index other relevant posts.
TopicResearch.insufficient: Fewer than 12 eligible records. Only descriptive results are shown.
TopicResearch.limitations: Counts describe this response. They cannot establish population views or regional differences.
TopicResearch.timelineHelp: Eligible posts and comments per UTC day represented in the response.
TopicResearch.linkOnly: Open records on their source site to read them. This view shows links, publication times and available language metadata.
TopicResearch.analysisOptional: Select fictional discussion analysis to view text-based results.
TopicResearch.analysisWithheld: Analysis of real text is paused pending verification of research-use permissions.
TopicResearch.analysisBasis: Analysis used {total} distinct English texts, including {posts} posts and {comments} comments.
TopicResearch.iterationLimit: The method reached its iteration limit.
TopicResearch.noAnalysisText: No texts met the analysis criteria.

topicStatuses.comparison: Both methods grouped the same eligible texts. Group numbers are specific to each method.
topicStatuses.nmf_only: The local MiniLM model was unavailable. TF-IDF + NMF results are shown.
topicStatuses.insufficient_texts: Grouping requires at least 12 eligible English texts.
topicStatuses.insufficient_variation: The eligible texts did not have enough variation to form two groups.

TopicResearch.expressionMethod: English wording rules count explicit expressions per text. Categories can overlap. These counts do not determine how a person actually feels.
TopicResearch.methodologyFictional: This is a fictional discussion sample. Models form two exploratory groups from distinct, bounded English texts. The evidence list identifies the texts used for both methods and the expression counts. Individual cluster assignments and AI interpretations are omitted.
TopicResearch.futureHelp: Validated analysis of expressed experiences, needs and emotions is reserved for eligible text under approved source-use and privacy conditions.

Dashboard.title: Analysis dashboard
Dashboard.intro: Explore online human experience and search interest.
Dashboard.notice: The charts in this section illustrate the interface with fictional text and search-interest data.

human.source: Fictional text data · Inspired by the CareerNet pilot
human.title: Human experience analysis
human.description: Topics, emotions, needs and experiences in writing about education and careers.
human.method: In these fixed fictional aggregates, each label counts the documents that carry it. Each share uses the selected cohort’s document total. A document can carry several labels, so shares can add up to more than 100%.
human.limit: Emotion labels reflect explicit expressions by fictional authors. These examples provide no evidence about psychological states, population prevalence, model performance or independent human evaluation.

caveats.general: A general sample from the fictional source frame. Shares use this cohort’s document count.
caveats.uncertainty-enriched: A sample enriched using fictional uncertainty cues. Its shares describe this cohort only.

search.source: Fictional time series · Inspired by Google Trends
search.title: Search interest analysis
search.description: A weekly relative interest index for a fictional search query.
search.coverage: {observed, number} of {weeks, number} weeks have values
search.chartLabel: Weekly fictional search interest. The line breaks at missing or suppressed weeks.
search.method: The fixed fictional series uses a relative index on a 0–100 scale. Missing and suppressed weeks have no numeric value and remain gaps in the line.
search.limit: The index contains no actual Google Trends measurements, counts of people or absolute search volumes. It is independent of the text cohorts and cannot establish causation between the two views.

states.invalid: The demo response did not match the expected contract.
states.empty: There is no demo data to display.
states.noCategories: There are no categories in this group.

LocalAnalysis.title: Analyze texts
LocalAnalysis.intro: Explore topic groups in a small collection of English texts with TF-IDF + NMF or MiniLM + K-means.
LocalAnalysis.inputHelp: Enter {min, number}–{max, number} texts, one per line, up to {chars, number} characters each. The application does not store the texts. Use fictional or appropriately de-identified test texts.
LocalAnalysis.resultSummary: {count, number} texts, {k, number} requested topic groups.
LocalAnalysis.nmfHelp: NMF uses word patterns. The terms shown are recurring words with high weights in this topic.
LocalAnalysis.minilmHelp: K-means groups MiniLM text vectors. The terms shown are lexical descriptors computed afterward from the assigned texts.
LocalAnalysis.agreementValue: Adjusted Rand index (ARI): {ari} across {count, number} texts assigned by both methods.
LocalAnalysis.agreementUnavailable: There are too few shared assignments or populated groups to report ARI.
LocalAnalysis.agreementHelp: ARI compares how the same texts are grouped, accounting for chance agreement. Topic accuracy requires independent thematic evaluation.
LocalAnalysis.unassigned: {count, plural, one {# text could not be assigned.} other {# texts could not be assigned.}}
LocalAnalysis.iterationLimit: The model reached its iteration limit. Interpret this grouping with extra care.
LocalAnalysis.limits: Group numbers are arbitrary and sizes describe only the submitted texts. A keyword must be in the permitted vocabulary and recur in at least three distinct texts in its group. The topics require human interpretation.

signals.title: Expressed Emotion, Need and Experience Signals
signals.denominator: Based on all {count, number} submitted texts.
signals.interpretation: Exploratory English phrase rules count each text at most once per category. A text can count in several categories. An unmarked text may still contain an emotion, need or experience. These counts describe matched expressions and provide no validated predictions or clinical assessments.

errors.tooLarge: Use at most 8,000 characters per document, 100,000 per collection and 256 KiB per request. Each document must be segmentable within the processing limits.
errors.invalidInput: The local service rejected the input. Check the text lines and group count.
errors.insufficientVariation: The texts contain too little distinct vocabulary for this group count. Try more varied texts or select two groups.
errors.busy: An analysis is already running. Try again in a moment.
errors.modelUnavailable: The verified local MiniLM model could not be loaded. Check the local model setup, or select TF-IDF + NMF.
errors.unavailable: Local analysis is unavailable. Check that the local API is running with analysis enabled.

TrendsResearch.title: Google Trends Research API
TrendsResearch.source: Google Trends Research API · Authorized local series
TrendsResearch.fictional: Fictional adapter test · No Google API data
TrendsResearch.withheld: No verified local series is available. The dashboard has made no Google query.
TrendsResearch.scale: Search interest in original API units
TrendsResearch.chartLabel: Search-interest time series with gaps for missing and suppressed values
TrendsResearch.limits: Search interest describes relative search activity. It provides no absolute search counts or direct measurement of emotion, population experience, or causation. A single query covers a narrow part of search behavior.
TrendsResearch.alignment: Comparisons with other sources require aligned geography, time periods, and definitions. This series is displayed separately from the CareerNet text results.

Research.title: Research Findings
Research.sample: The first case study used {questions, number} reviewed English questions about careers.
Research.comparison: TF-IDF + NMF and MiniLM + K-means compared
Research.scale: Bars show the positive ARI values observed here on a 0–1 scale.
Research.ari: The adjusted Rand index (ARI) compares how the same questions are grouped and accounts for agreement expected by chance. A value of 1 means identical groupings, and a value near 0 indicates chance-level agreement. Classification accuracy is outside the scope of this experiment.
Research.stability: Stability shows how similar the clusters were across {repetitions, number} subsampling repetitions, each using about {share} of the sample.
Research.observed: Both methods were more stable with two clusters (k = 2) in the main experiment. Thematic validity and method superiority require further evidence.
Research.review: A first reviewer assigned the labels. A second reviewer independently assessed {questions, number} purposefully selected questions. Agreement varied by category. This small overlap sample is insufficient to establish general inter-rater reliability.
Research.limits: This small, selected English-language career sample describes the pilot only. Population estimates, clinical anxiety detection and causal inference are outside its scope.
Research.attribution: Hissiyat selected a sample from the dataset and compared methods. The analysis and interpretations belong to the Hissiyat project. Attribution implies no publisher endorsement.

NotFound.title: Page not found
NotFound.description: The page you are looking for does not exist.
